notes: Phone push (thread L6): the APNs token registered with every paired host, one Settings row, notification taps landing on the card. ios/TempCodeClient Push/PushRegistrar.swift keeps the device token, the switch and what each host holds (a host hears the token when its socket opens and again only when it changes; off unregisters everywhere; remote.push.activity hands a Live Activity token over), PushTarget reads the hub's tc payload and the activity's tempcode://thread URL, and the row's word comes from the switch, the permission, the token and the hosts' relay states; EnvironmentClient tells the registrar at every open and forgets a removed host, ClientRegistry owns it. In the app, Push/PushDelegate.swift is the UIApplicationDelegate adaptor and notification-centre delegate (token callbacks, a tap routed as a PushTarget, foreground delivery silent for the thread on screen, the APNs environment read off the embedded provisioning profile), Push/NavigationRouter.swift carries the pending route and the visible thread, RootView replaces the Home stack with the thread on its row for a tap or a tempcode:// URL, ThreadScreen reports itself visible, SettingsView gains the Notifications switch with its state beside it, AppModel asks for permission once and registers for a token. TC_TEST_ROUTE=notification with TC_TEST_NOTIFICATION='title part|seq' feeds the delegate a hub-shaped payload; scripts/ios-sim-proof.sh's push set proves the tap lands on row 41 of the 2,000-row thread and shoots the row (in all). The capability test now expects the four remote.push.* rows at read. Package tests 152 (PushTarget, PushRegistrar).
